Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the annual DCAT (Dynamic Capital Adequacy Testing) stress-and-scenario program and the s.369 duty to report material adverse matters; the Capital Model Actuary executes the scenario runs under her direction and the Chief Risk Officer owns the s.369(2)/(3) escalation chain.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Companies Act, S.C. 1991, c. 47, ss. 357-358 (appointment/notice of Appointed Actuary), s. 368 (report to directors on financial condition), s. 369 (duty to report material adverse matters), read against the current OSFI Guideline A: Dynamic Capital Adequacy Testing and Guideline E-15 (Appointed Actuary), re-read at each DCAT cycle kickoff (rep: Canada, OSFI-supervised federal entities)

In-scope processes.value: Annual DCAT stress-and-scenario testing cycle — from scenario design and modeling through Appointed Actuary materiality assessment, the s.369 CEO/CFO/Board escalation ladder, and the s.368 Report on the Financial Condition delivered ahead of the annual meeting — for every federally regulated life and P&C entity in the group

In-scope systems.value: Scenario projections run in the actuarial modeling platform; capital results consolidated into the LICAT/MCT capital forecast in Anaplan; escalation and Board records held in the board portal and the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: DCAT / Stress and Scenario Testing Procedure aligned to OSFI Guideline A — scenario universe selection, model refresh, ruin-scenario computation, materiality assessment against the documented threshold, and the s.369(1)-(3) escalation script with named recipients and timeframes

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and the Board Risk Committee; reviewed annually ahead of the DCAT kickoff and on any update to OSFI Guideline A or the CIA Standards of Practice for DCAT

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: DCAT report and s.368 Report on the Financial Condition must be finalized in time to reach shareholders/policyholders at least 21 days before the annual meeting; any s.369(1) finding starts a 10-business-day CEO/CFO response clock, escalating to the Board and then the Superintendent if unresolved

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal milestone alerts at T-90/T-45/T-21 days ahead of the annual meeting date for the financial condition report notice, plus a T+10-business-day tickler on every open s.369(1) CEO/CFO memo

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: DCAT report, scenario run outputs, s.369 memos and responses, board minutes extract and the signed financial condition report retained a minimum of 7 years in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by entity, reporting year and scenario name

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed scenario, late CEO/CFO or Board escalation, or a financial condition report distributed inside the 21-day window is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Risk Officer signs off every exception remediation and, jointly with General Counsel, any decision to self-report a missed s.369 escalation to OSFI

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every DCAT scenario run (base, plausible adverse, ruin and combined) logged for the current reporting year by entity, plus every s.369 memo, Board escalation record and Superintendent notice raised in the same period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Re-performed capital ratio trajectories must match the reported DCAT output within 1 LICAT/MCT point; zero tolerance on a material s.369 finding that was not escalated on schedule or a financial condition report distributed after the 21-day pre-AGM deadline

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual, run after the Appointed Actuary signs the DCAT report and before the Board formally accepts it, so any re-performance exception can still be corrected ahead of the annual meeting

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or signed any of the sampled DCAT scenario runs or escalation memos

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual DCAT test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository alongside the DCAT evidence package

Regulator-ready documentation.value: DCAT report, scenario run log, s.369 escalation trail and financial condition report, presentable to OSFI within 10 business days of a supervisory request

Regulator response path.value: Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel own any OSFI inquiry or follow-up arising from a s.369(3) Superintendent notice; Appointed Actuary provides the technical DCAT record

checklist.step: Scope the annual DCAT program and confirm the scenario universe
actions: Pull the prior year's DCAT report and the current edition of OSFI Guideline A: Dynamic Capital Adequacy Testing from the model governance repository and confirm no scope changes since last cycle.
Confirm the base scenario assumptions (economic outlook, business plan) with the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Financial Officer, sourced from the current 3-year business plan.

List the minimum plausible adverse scenario categories required by Guideline A — a severe interest-rate/recession scenario, a mortality or morbidity shock, a lapse/new-business shock, and a combined scenario — and add any company-specific ruin scenario.
Confirm the federally regulated entities in scope and each one's year-end reporting date.
Log the DCAT project plan and milestone dates in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the scope, base assumptions and adverse scenario list are confirmed and logged with milestone dates for every in-scope entity.

checklist.step: Refresh the actuarial model to the current valuation basis
actions: In the actuarial modeling platform, roll the in-force model forward to the valuation date and reconcile policy counts and reserves to the ERP/General ledger extract.
Refresh the economic scenario generator's assumptions (interest rate curve, equity and credit spreads) from the investment/treasury function.
Validate the refreshed model's output against last quarter's actuals within a 2% reserve tolerance before running any stress scenario.
Have the Reserving Actuary confirm the opening reserves feeding the model tie to the year-end actuarial valuation.
Log the model change and validation result in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the model is rolled forward, reconciled to the GL and to the year-end valuation within tolerance, and the change is logged.

checklist.step: Run the base scenario and each adverse scenario
actions: Execute the base scenario projection over the required planning horizon and capture the projected LICAT/MCT capital ratio for each projection year.
Execute each adverse scenario, capturing the ratio trajectory and the point, if any, where it breaches the internal target ratio or OSFI's supervisory target (LICAT/MCT 100%).
Run a combined scenario stacking two or more adverse triggers to represent a 'worst reasonable' outcome.
Save every run's output, assumption set and a run ID/timestamp into the model governance repository.
checklist.done: base, each adverse, and one combined scenario are run, and every output is saved with a traceable run ID.

checklist.step: Quantify the capital and solvency impact of each ruin scenario
actions: For each scenario, compute the capital ratio impact and, where the ratio falls below the regulatory or internal target, compute the time-to-breach and the capital shortfall in dollars.
Identify plausible management actions (reinsurance, reduced new business, capital raise, dividend deferral) and re-run the scenario with the action applied to show the mitigated result.
Ask the Reserving Actuary to independently confirm the starting reserves used in each ruin scenario.
Summarize results in a scenario-impact table by projection year and scenario.
checklist.done: every adverse scenario has a computed capital impact, a time-to-breach where relevant, and a mitigated re-run, summarized in the impact table.

checklist.step: Draft the DCAT report per OSFI Guideline A structure
actions: Draft the DCAT report in the CIA/OSFI-prescribed structure: introduction, base scenario, plausible adverse scenarios, ruin scenarios, and the Appointed Actuary's opinion on the overall financial condition.
State explicitly whether any scenario reveals a material adverse effect on the company's financial condition within the meaning of s. 369.
Have the Reserving Actuary and Capital Model Actuary peer-review the draft against the underlying model runs.
Route the draft for technical sign-off within the actuarial function before it is used to assess the s. 369 duty.
checklist.done: the DCAT report is drafted in the prescribed structure, states the s.369 materiality position, and is peer-reviewed.

checklist.step: Assess whether any finding triggers the s.369 duty to report material matters
actions: Test each adverse finding against the company's documented materiality threshold (e.g., a scenario that breaches supervisory target capital within the planning horizon, or a going-concern indicator).
Where a finding is material, draft the written memo to the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer required by s. 369(1), stating the matter and the corrective action believed necessary.
Where no finding is material, document the negative assertion and its basis in the DCAT report.
Consult Regulatory Counsel on any threshold call that is not unambiguous.
checklist.done: every adverse finding has a documented materiality call, and any material finding has a drafted s.369(1) memo.

checklist.step: Deliver the s.369 report to the CEO and CFO and track their response
actions: Deliver the written memo to the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer by hand and email, logging the delivery date — this starts the clock on the company's duty to rectify.
Request a written rectification plan and timeline from the CEO/CFO within 10 business days.
If no adequate response is received or the CEO/CFO indicate the matter will not be rectified, prepare the s. 369(2) escalation memo to the Board of Directors.
Log every communication and response in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the CEO/CFO memo is delivered and dated, and a 10-business-day response is logged or a Board escalation memo is prepared.

checklist.step: Escalate unresolved material matters to the Board of Directors
actions: Upload the s.369(2) escalation memo and the supporting DCAT extracts to the board portal ahead of the next scheduled Board or Audit/Risk Committee meeting.
Present the finding, the CEO/CFO response (or lack of one), and the recommended corrective action to the Board.
Record the Board's decision and any directed remediation timeline in the board minutes.
If the Board also fails to secure rectification, prepare the further escalation to the Superintendent of Financial Institutions required by s. 369(3).
checklist.done: the Board has reviewed the escalation memo, its decision is minuted, and a s.369(3) escalation is prepared if unresolved.

checklist.step: File the escalation with the OSFI Superintendent when the Board does not rectify
actions: Confirm with General Counsel that the Board-level escalation window closed without adequate rectification.
Draft the notice to the Superintendent describing the matter, the steps taken under s. 369(1) and (2), and the company's current position.
Log the correspondence and OSFI's acknowledgment in the Internal Regulatory System's OSFI correspondence log.
Track any resulting supervisory follow-up (targeted review, letter of expectation) to closure.
checklist.done: the s.369(3) notice, where triggered, is filed with OSFI, acknowledged, and logged with any follow-up tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Finalize the Appointed Actuary's Report on the Financial Condition of the Company
actions: Incorporate the DCAT results and any s.369 findings, with their disposition, into the annual Report on the Financial Condition required under s. 368.
State the actuary's opinion on the adequacy of the company's capital and reserves and any qualifications.
Have the Chief Financial Officer review the report for consistency with the audited financial statements.
Sign and date the final report.
checklist.done: the s.368 Report on the Financial Condition is finalized, CFO-reviewed, and signed.

checklist.step: Route the report for the 21-day pre-annual-meeting notice
actions: Confirm the annual meeting of shareholders/policyholders date from the corporate calendar.
Calculate the notice deadline as 21 days before that date and diarize it in the board portal with a T-7 reminder.
Distribute the Appointed Actuary's Report on the Financial Condition to shareholders/policyholders (or make it available per the company's governance practice) no later than the 21-day deadline.
Log the distribution date and method as governance evidence.
checklist.done: the financial condition report is distributed on or before the 21-day pre-annual-meeting deadline, with distribution date logged.

checklist.step: Obtain Board acceptance of the DCAT report and the financial condition opinion
actions: Place the DCAT report and the s.368 financial condition report on the Board (or Audit/Risk Committee) agenda via the board portal.
Record Board questions, the Appointed Actuary's responses, and the Board's formal acceptance or requested revisions in the minutes.
Confirm any Board-directed management action is assigned an owner and a target date.
File the signed minutes extract with the DCAT report package.
checklist.done: the Board's acceptance (or requested revisions) is minuted and any directed action has an owner and date.

checklist.step: Feed the DCAT results into the capital plan and LICAT/MCT forecast
actions: Load the scenario capital-ratio trajectories into the capital planning model in Anaplan alongside the business plan.
Update the contingency capital plan (recapitalization triggers, reinsurance triggers, dividend policy) to reflect any new ruin scenario finding.
Confirm with the CFO/Capital Management function that the next LICAT/MCT return to OSFI reflects the updated assumptions.
Record the updated capital plan version in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the capital plan and next LICAT/MCT forecast in Anaplan reflect the current DCAT results and any ruin-scenario finding.

checklist.step: Log any procedural exception in the DCAT and escalation cycle
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any step that missed its internal deadline — a late escalation memo, or Board sign-off delayed past the 21-day notice deadline.
Assign a root cause and an owner and set a remediation date.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer of any issue touching the s.369 escalation chain.
Carry open issues into the next year's DCAT cycle as a mandatory pre-check.
checklist.done: every procedural exception has a tracker issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, carried forward as a pre-check.

checklist.step: Retain the full DCAT and escalation evidence package
actions: Assemble the DCAT report, scenario run outputs, s.369 memos and responses, board minutes extract, and the signed financial condition report into a single evidence package.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year and entity name.
Apply the minimum 7-year retention label matching OSFI's expectation and the company's document retention policy.
Confirm the package is indexed and retrievable by entity, reporting year and scenario name.
checklist.done: the DCAT evidence package is filed, retention-labelled for 7 years, and retrievable by entity, year and scenario name.

testing.step: Build the population of DCAT scenarios and escalation events for the cycle
actions: Extract from the model governance repository every DCAT scenario run — base, adverse, ruin and combined — logged for the current reporting year, by entity.
Extract every s.369 memo, Board escalation record and Superintendent notice raised in the same period.
Reconcile the run count to the DCAT report's scenario list and the escalation count to the board minutes; resolve any gap before sampling.
testing.done: the scenario and escalation population is reconciled to the DCAT report and board minutes and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the DCAT model inputs to the year-end valuation and general ledger
actions: Trace the opening reserves and in-force data used in the DCAT model to the year-end actuarial valuation and to the GL extract.
Confirm the economic assumptions used (rate curve, equity returns) match the source provided by the investment/treasury function on the run date.
Flag any unreconciled variance above the 2% tolerance as an exception.
testing.done: model inputs are traced to the valuation and GL, with any variance above tolerance logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select a sample of scenarios and independently re-perform the run
actions: Select the base scenario plus a minimum of two adverse scenarios, including any scenario that showed a capital breach, for independent re-performance.
In the actuarial modeling platform, re-run each selected scenario from the documented assumption set without reference to the original output.
Compare the re-performed capital ratio trajectory to the original within a 1-point LICAT/MCT tolerance; any larger variance is logged as an exception requiring root cause.
Record the seed assumption set and run date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: each sampled scenario has an independent re-performance note, and any variance beyond tolerance is logged with root cause.

testing.step: Recompute the capital ratio and time-to-breach maths for the worst adverse scenario
actions: Independently recompute the projected LICAT/MCT ratio for the most severe scenario using the reported starting capital, projected required capital and projected available capital.
Recompute the time-to-breach against the supervisory (100%) and the company's internal target ratio.
Compare the recomputed figures to the DCAT report's stated figures and log any discrepancy.
testing.done: the worst-scenario capital ratio and time-to-breach are independently recomputed and reconciled to the DCAT report.

testing.step: Test the s.369 materiality call against the documented threshold
actions: Read the company's documented materiality threshold for 'material adverse effect' and apply it independently to each scenario finding in the sample.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's decision to report, or not report, each finding under s. 369 matches counsel's independent application of the threshold.
Treat any finding that should have been reported to the CEO/CFO but was not as a reportable exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled materiality call is independently re-applied and confirmed, with any mismatch logged as a reportable exception.

testing.step: Trace the escalation trail's dates against the statutory sequence
actions: For every reported material matter, confirm the CEO/CFO delivery date, any Board escalation date, and any Superintendent notice date appear in strict s. 369(1) then (2) then (3) order.
Confirm the Board escalation occurred only where the logged CEO/CFO response was inadequate or absent.
Confirm any Superintendent notice was filed and acknowledged in the Internal Regulatory System's OSFI correspondence log.
testing.done: the escalation trail dates for every material matter follow the correct statutory sequence, with any break logged.

testing.step: Verify the 21-day pre-annual-meeting notice deadline was met
actions: Pull the annual meeting date from the corporate calendar and confirm the calculated 21-day deadline in the board portal reminder log.
Confirm the distribution date of the Report on the Financial Condition to shareholders/policyholders is on or before that deadline.
Log any late distribution as a compliance exception regardless of whether the Board later accepted the report.
testing.done: the 21-day pre-annual-meeting notice deadline is confirmed met or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm evidence completeness and retention labeling
actions: Open the filed DCAT evidence package in the compliance evidence repository and confirm it contains the DCAT report, scenario run outputs, s.369 memos, board minutes extract and financial condition report.
Confirm the retention label matches the minimum 7-year policy and the package is indexed by entity, reporting year and scenario name.
Flag any missing artifact as an exception.
testing.done: the DCAT evidence package is confirmed complete, correctly retention-labelled and indexed, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found in re-performance, reconciliation, materiality testing, escalation-timing testing or evidence testing.
Assign a root cause (model refresh error, assumption not updated, escalation delayed, threshold misapplied) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed or late s.369 escalation, notify General Counsel to assess a self-report to OSFI.
Carry every open exception into next year's DCAT test plan as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment for next cycle.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Compute the exception rate against the pass/fail threshold and classify the DCAT program as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have an independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled re-performances sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, exception rate and any open s.369 matters to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository alongside the DCAT evidence package.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, and results are reported to the Board Risk Committee.
